1.why: All 11 screens are static cards with no animations, carousels, or modal pop-ups; the layout is plain and uncluttered.

2.why: Headings are large and dark blue and the primary action button is a high-contrast filled button, though the large dark 'Logs' panel competes visually with the real task.

3.why: Each screen shows one short form, but the user must pick the right tab among 'Request reset / Enter code / Sign in' and hunt the mock code out of the technical Logs panel.

4.why: She must track a multi-step flow (request → copy a 40-character token → set password with 12-char/uppercase/symbol rules → find a 6-digit MFA code in the log → accept conditions), which is a lot of rules and steps to hold.

5.why: No password manager hint, autofill affordance, 'remember me' checkbox, or show-password toggle appears on any of the password/code fields.

6.why: Nothing saved or familiar is surfaced — no remembered contact, no masked account hint, only opaque random tokens like 'fd-83gNz4_xjEST1_5TJx8FCVaOmFDaqFRGBzJhIZCE'.

7.why: Instructional sentences are short, plain and high-contrast, although the Logs text uses technical wording ('SIMULATED MFA', 'token=').

8.why: No error state is shown anywhere in the 11 screenshots; only success messages appear, so no problem-plus-fix messaging is evidenced.

9.why: Guidance is descriptive only ('Use an email-style contact value', 'At least 12 characters…') with no concrete sample input or worked example shown.

10.why: The available routes (password sign-in, reset code, security code) are labelled clearly, but there is no face/biometric option and the difference between 'Enter code' and 'Sign in' is not explained.

11.why: Each step presents a single form with one primary button plus only three navigation tabs, so choices are few at any moment.

12.why: Green bold confirmations appear after key actions ('reset instructions have been prepared', 'Security check complete', 'Updated privacy conditions have been accepted') plus a log trail, though the password-saved step shows no confirmation.

13.why: Every panel carries a short explanatory tip line and a persistent 'Stay safe' guidance banner about never sharing codes.

14.why: There are no back, cancel, retry or resend controls; codes are one-time and expire in 15 minutes, so recovering from a mistake means restarting via the tabs.

15.why: Header, tab bar, safety banner, single white card and Logs panel keep identical placement, typography and colour across all 11 steps.
